{"parentUuid":"68b082c4-a8e9-401b-850a-fc3542885475","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"4c73442b-0b28-469a-88d0-ad99fafb6f07","agentId":"a752d22dfcc1500d3","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<command-message>crucible</command-message>\n<command-name>crucible</command-name>\n<skill-format>true</skill-format>"},{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main/.claude/skills/crucible\n\n# CRUCIBLE — operating the engine\n\nCRUCIBLE turns an authorized seed URL into **oracle-confirmed** findings, reasons over them,\nand produces auditable reports — inside a fail-closed safety stack. Its whole value is one\nrule; internalize it before anything else:\n\n> **A claim is a FACT only when a deterministic oracle fires over data a real target\n> produced.** You (the LLM) ADVISE where to look and what a result might mean; the oracle\n> CONFIRMS. Nothing else — not your confidence, not a critic's endorsement, not a plausible\n> story — promotes a claim to a fact.\n\nThe standing doctrine every reasoning call operates under is\n[framework/cognitive/metacognition.md](../../../framework/cognitive/metacognition.md) (it is\ninjected into every LLM system prompt). The full architecture — agents, event spine, veracity\nlayer, learning/metacognition core, safety stack — is\n[framework/v2/docs/CRUCIBLE-AI.md](../../../framework/v2/docs/CRUCIBLE-AI.md). The binding\nconstitution is [CLAUDE.md](../../../CLAUDE.md); never relax scope, destruction, evidence, or\nhonesty rules.\n\n## The invariants (never violate these)\n\n1. **Oracle authority.** Only a fired oracle confirms. Critics/RL/reflection/self-consistency\n   may only *advise, re-rank, defer, or abstain* — never promote a finding or override the oracle.\n2. **Coverage.** Never silently skip an authorized attack surface. Learning and reflection\n   *deprioritise* (re-rank / defer); they never gate a surface out.\n3. **Prove by re-execution.** A finding is a fact only if its retained `oracle_context`\n   re-fires. The veracity firewall (`framework/v2/veracity/`) re-runs proofs; it can only demote.\n4. **Non-circular learning.** An EXPLOITABLE label needs ≥2 independent corroborating oracle\n   kinds; a silent oracle is never auto-labelled a false positive.\n5. **Refuse honestly, fail closed.** Decline to conclude what you cannot ground; record every\n   refusal as evidence. Hard limits (scope, authorization, destruction, real user data) are\n   inviolable — when unsure, stop and ask.\n6. **Determinism + append-only.** No wallclock/global-rng in learning/reward math; the event\n   spine is append-only (supersede, never edit).\n\n## Structured workflows\n\n### Run an authorized engagement (end-to-end, gated)\n1. Confirm the active target's `targets/<slug>/charter.md` authorizes it (constitution §II).\n2. `python3 -m framework.v2 engage <slug> <seed-url> [--recon] [--spine]`\n   — crawls, audits, confirms via oracles, chains attack paths, scores confidence, and\n   (with `--spine`) mirrors the whole run onto the immutable blackboard event stream.\n   (`--strict-evidence` is a **`scan`**-only flag, below — not an `engage` flag.)\n3. Every request passes the full gate chain; an out-of-scope seed or tripped kill-switch\n   refuses *before* traffic and is recorded as a `refusal` event.\n\n### Loopback-only quick scan\n`python3 -m framework.v2 scan http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ --format json|sarif|html [--strict-evidence]`\n— the export states each finding's **live grounding** (fact / ungrounded / contradicted);\n`--strict-evidence` withholds non-fact findings from the rendered doc but keeps them in\n`--reverifiable-out`.\n\n### Re-verify a report (prove-don't-guess, offline)\n`python3 -m framework.v2 verify <report.json>` re-runs each finding's retained `oracle_context`.\n`python3 -m framework.v2 evidence ...` builds/verifies signed, hash-linked evidence certificates\n(and, with report claims bound in, fails closed when a report sentence has no backing evidence).\n\n### Inspect / audit the event spine\nThe blackboard (`framework/v2/agents/blackboard.py`) is the one append-only, typed, provenance-\nlinked event stream. Replay it with `Blackboard.replay(engagement=..., since_id=...)`.\nCryptographic tamper-evidence: `framework/v2/agents/spine_chain.py`\n(`build_spine_chain` / `sign_spine_head` / `verify_spine_head`).\n\n### Recon / intel, memory, self-improvement\n`python3 -m framework.v2 intel ...` (OSINT into the shared world-model; gated egress),\n`memory ...` (cross-engagement priors — never fabricate a score), `improve ...`\n(authorise-not-apply — it never self-applies a change).\n\n### Read-only operator console\n`python3 -m framework.v2 console` — loopback, read-only, zero-impact operator UI over the run.\n\n## What NOT to do\n- Do not build detection-evasion / identity-rotation / stay-hidden-from-defenders capability —\n  CRUCIBLE is correlatable and authorized by doctrine (constitution §VI).\n- Do not let any learned/critic/LLM signal enter the deterministic oracle/SCE/calibration inputs\n  or promote a finding.\n- Do not attack third parties (payment/IdP/CDN) — test only the operator's integration with them.\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"uuid":"cd5e350e-0016-4e3d-b806-a865c0387d89","timestamp":"2026-07-19T06:47:23.600Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

a deliberate trust-narrowing inside the widening.\n205\t        #     Reject non-finite/non-positive BEFORE the min() (min(nan,300)=nan → a never-expiring session).\n206\t        try:\n207\t            raw_ttl = float(request.get(\"ttl_seconds\", MAX_DEVICE_TTL))\n208\t        except (TypeError, ValueError):\n209\t            return self._refuse_arm(request, \"invalid ttl\")\n210\t        if not math.isfinite(raw_ttl) or raw_ttl <= 0:\n211\t            return self._refuse_arm(request, \"non-finite or non-positive ttl\")\n212\t        ttl = min(raw_ttl, MAX_DEVICE_TTL)\n213\t        sid = uuid.uuid4().hex\n214\t        # The record's AUTHORIZATION is the verified device signature — self-verifying vs the owner-signed\n215\t        # device ledger; inject NOTHING\n271\t        token = sha256_hex(f\"{self.session.session_id}|{tool}|{args}\".encode(\"utf-8\"))\n272\t        seq = self.store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"gesture\", actor=\"PERCEPTION\",\n273\t                                payload={\"signal\": ACTION_SIGNAL, \"decision\": \"queued\",\n274\t                                         \"status\": \"awaiting-approval\", \"tier\": tier.label(),\n275\t                                         \"tool\": tool, \"action_token\": token, \"args\": args,\n276\t                                         \"subject\": f\"gesture action {tool} (awaiting approval)\"})\n277\t        return {\"injected\": False, \"queued\": seq, \"tier\": tier.label(), \"tool\": tool, \"action_token\": token}\n278\t\n279\t    def _inject(self, intent: GestureIntent) -> None:\n280\t        b = self.backend\n281\t        if intent.kind == \"move\" or intent.kind == \"drag\":\n282\t            b.move(intent.dx, intent.dy)\n283\t        elif intent.kind == \"click\":\n284\t            b.click()\n285\t        elif intent.kind == \"scroll_left\":\n286\t            b.scroll(-1, 0)\n287\t        elif intent.kind == \"scroll_right\":\n288\t            b.scroll(1, 0)\n289\t"}]},"uuid":"b3b1523d-3e6b-4348-a8af-18b8aa369b8f","timestamp":"2026-07-19T06:47:42.925Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"9e95b5f2-364d-4618-959a-b773c1b9a9d8","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

{"parentUuid":"88b6b2ec-7df7-403d-be3e-dc0b88fa4ddd","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"4c73442b-0b28-469a-88d0-ad99fafb6f07","agentId":"a752d22dfcc1500d3","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_013wYUNGGQWJPBG36JbQasdE","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"The kill switch (SIGIL §5) — a single latch that halts the agent mesh while leaving perception and\n2\tmemory-read (A0 observe) alive. State is append-only on the spine.\n3\t\n4\tASYMMETRIC AUTHENTICATION (Phase 6 red-pen RP-2): halting is always the safe direction, so ANY\n5\tengage event halts (a nuisance forged-engage is at worst a fail-safe DoS). UN-halting is the\n6\tdangerous direction, so a RELEASE is honored ONLY if it is signed by the owner key and verifies\n7\tagainst the trusted pubkey — a forged release can never revive a halted mesh. Read fresh per decision\n8\tso a release (or engage) takes effect immediately.\"\"\"\n9\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n10\t\n11\tfrom typing import Optional\n12\t\n13\tfrom .authn import signed_payload, verify_signed\n14\tfrom .identity import owner_keypair, owner_pubkey\n15\t\n16\tSIGNAL = \"governor.killswitch\"\n17\t_CORE = (\"signal\", \"state\")\n18\t\n19\t\n20\tclass KillSwitch:\n21\t    def __init__(self, store, *, owner_key=None, trusted_pubkey: Optional[str] = None):\n22\t        self.store = store\n23\t        self.owner_key = owner_key if owner_key is not None else owner_keypair()\n24\t        self.trusted_pubkey = trusted_pubkey if trusted_pubkey is not None else owner_pubkey()\n25\t\n26\t    def engage(self, *, by: str = \"owner\", reason: str = \"\") -> int:\n27\t        core = {\"signal\": SIGNAL, \"state\": \"engaged\"}\n28\t        payload = {**signed_payload(core, self.owner_key), \"by\": by, \"reason\": reason,\n29\t                   \"tier\": \"A0\", \"decision\": \"auto\"}\n30\t        return self.store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"governor\", actor=\"WARDEN\", payload=payload)\n31\t\n32\t    def release(self, *, by: str = \"owner\", reason: str = \"\") -> int:\n33\t        core = {\"signal\": SIGNAL, \"state\": \"released\"}\n34\t        payload = {**signed_payload(core, self.owner_key), \"by\": by, \"reason\": reason,\n35\t                   \"tier\": \"A0\", \"decision\": \"auto\"}\n36\t        return self.store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"governor\", actor=\"WARDEN\", payload=payload)\n37\t\n38\t    def is_engaged(self) -> bool:\n39\t        engaged = False\n40\t        for r in self.store.iter_records():\n41\t            p = r.payload\n42\t            if p.get(\"signal\") != SIGNAL:\n43\t                continue\n44\t            state = p.get(\"state\")\n45\t            if state == \"engaged\":\n46\t                engaged = True                      # honor ANY engage — halting is fail-safe\n47\t            elif state == \"released\" and verify_signed(p, _CORE, self.trusted_pubkey):\n48\t                engaged = False                     # only an OWNER-SIGNED release un-halts (fail-closed)\n49\t        return engaged\n50\t"}]},"uuid":"ebecf98f-c1ef-4162-981d-d1b0f454e3b2","timestamp":"2026-07-19T06:47:47.865Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"88b6b2ec-7df7-403d-be3e-dc0b88fa4ddd","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

{"parentUuid":"265f6ccf-c6db-474a-be08-3bfbaf0bdd9e","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"4c73442b-0b28-469a-88d0-ad99fafb6f07","agentId":"a752d22dfcc1500d3","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Jhpmvz3jegA9AtsD9PGJsT","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"BridgeDaemon (Phase 7, WS-D D-v) — the desktop-side API the phone talks to over WireGuard. It\n2\treuses the owner-signed cores: the queue (`approvals.pending` with the authorized-device set), a\n3\tDEVICE-signed approval (accepted only while that device is authorized), a PANIC halt (any engage is\n4\tfail-safe), and a KERNEL command relay (`KernelDispatch` → the same WARDEN gate as voice/UI).\n5\t\n6\tThis module is the bridge LIBRARY CORE + API (the doctrine + crypto). The network TRANSPORT — an\n7\tHTTP server over WireGuard, reusing the WS-C two-plane server pattern bound to a `bind_ok` address —\n8\tis a documented NEXT slice, not shipped here. `bind_ok` is the bind predicate that transport MUST\n9\tuse: loopback or a PRIVATE (WireGuard) address only — NEVER 0.0.0.0 / a public address.\"\"\"\n10\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n11\t\n12\timport ipaddress\n13\tfrom typing import List, Optional\n14\t\n15\tfrom ..spine.store import SpineStore\n16\t\n17\t\n18\t_CGNAT4 = ipaddress.ip_network(\"100.64.0.0/10\")   # carrier-grade NAT — the range Tailscale assigns tailnet IPs\n19\t_DEDUP_WINDOW = 2048                               # bound the replay-dedup scan to the most recent N records\n20\t\n21\t\n22\tdef bind_ok(addr: str) -> bool:\n23\t    \"\"\"True iff `addr` is safe to bind: loopback, a PRIVATE (e.g. WireGuard) address, or the CGNAT range\n24\t    Tailscale uses — never 0.0.0.0 / a public / an unspecified address.\"\"\"\n25\t    try:\n26\t        ip = ipaddress.ip_address(addr)\n27\t    except ValueError:\n28\t        return False\n29\t    if ip.is_unspecified:                          # 0.0.0.0 / :: → refuse\n30\t        return False\n31\t    return ip.is_loopback or ip.is_private or (ip.version == 4 and ip in _CGNAT4)\n32\t\n33\t\n34\tclass BridgeDaemon:\n35\t    def __init__(self, store: Optional[SpineStore] = None, *, trusted_pubkey: Optional[str] = None):\n36\t        from ..governor.identity import owner_pubkey\n37\t        self.store = store or SpineStore()\n38\t        # the owner trust anchor — the persisted identity by default (injectable for tests)\n39\t        self.trusted_pubkey = trusted_pubkey if trusted_pubkey is not None else owner_pubkey()\n40\t\n41\t    def _authorized(self):\n42\t        from ..mesh import authorized_devices\n43\t        return authorized_devices(self.store, self.trusted_pubkey)\n44\t\n45\t    def pending(self) -> List[dict]:\n46\t        \"\"\"The phone-facing queue — minimal fields only (no subject leaks over the tunnel).\"\"\"\n47\t        from ..agents.approvals import pending\n48\t        items = pending(self.store, self.trusted_pubkey, extra_pubkeys=self._authorized())\n49\t        return [{\"seq\": r.seq, \"tier\": r.payload.get(\"tier\"), \"kind\": r.kind} for r in items]\n50\t\n51\t    def recall(self, subject: str) -> Optional[dict]:\n52\t        \"\"\"Read-only remote RECALL — \"where did I last see X?\" — answered from the owner's own\n53\t        GROUNDED on-screen OCR history. Returns the perception-recall provenance dict VERBATIM\n54\t        (seq/entry_hash/when/frame_sha256/quote) or None: A0, read-only, no VLM and no paraphrase —\n55\t        the served `quote` is the owner's verbatim captured OCR line, never an advisory VLM lead.\n56\t\n57\t        This surfaces the owner's own on-screen text over the tunnel, so it leaks MORE than\n58\t        `pending()`'s minimal {seq,tier,kind} fields. The network SERVER (a later slice) MUST\n59\t        therefore gate this behind an authorized-device (device-signed) read request; this daemon\n60\t        method is only the read-only core.\"\"\"\n61\t        from ..perception.recall import recall\n62\t        return recall(self.store, subject)\n63\t\n64\t    def submit_device_approval(self, payload: dict) -> int:\n65\t        \"\"\"Append a DEVICE-signed approval the phone produced — ONLY if the signing device is\n66\t        currently authorized AND the signature verifies (fail-closed). A rogue/revoked device or a\n67\t        forged signature is refused; the signed target_seq binds (no replay).\"\"\"\n68\t        from ..agents.approvals import SIGNAL as APPROVAL_SIGNAL\n69\t        from ..agents.approvals import verify_approval\n70\t\n71\t        class _Rec:\n72\t            def __init__(self, p): self.payload = p\n73\t        authorized = self._authorized()\n74\t        if payload.get(\"signal\") != APPROVAL_SIGNAL:\n75\t            raise ValueError(\"not an approval record\")\n76\t        if payload.get(\"pubkey\") not in authorized:\n77\t            raise ValueError(\"signing device is not authorized\")\n78\t        if not verify_approval(_Rec(payload), self.trusted_pubkey, extra_pubkeys=authorized):\n79\t            raise ValueError(\"approval signature invalid\")\n80\t        sig, tgt = payload.get(\"sig\"), payload.get(\"target_seq\")\n81\t        # Best-effort dedup OUTSIDE the append lock (a rare concurrent double-record is benign; holding the\n82\t        # lock across a scan would stall every writer), over a BOUNDED recent window (O(window), not\n83\t        # O(spine) — a flood is always recent, so the window catches it independent of `target_seq`).\n84\t        for r in self.store.tail(_DEDUP_WINDOW):\n85\t            p = r.payload\n86\t            if p.get(\"signal\") == APPROVAL_SIGNAL and p.get(\"pubkey\") == payload.get(\"pubkey\") and p.get(\"sig\") == sig:\n87\t                return r.seq                            # already recorded — idempotent\n88\t        return self.store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"mesh\", actor=\"DEVICE\",\n89\t                                 payload={**payload, \"tier\": \"A0\", \"decision\": \"auto\"}, supersedes_id=tgt)\n90\t\n91\t    def submit_arm_request(self, request: dict) -> int:\n92\t        \"\"\"Record a DEVICE-signed gesture arm request (the transport layer) — ONLY if the signing device\n93\t        is authorized AND the signature verifies (fail-closed, mirrors submit_device_approval). The live\n94\t        SessionGate RE-VERIFIES and enforces freshness / kill-switch / single-session / TTL when it\n95\t        consumes this via `arm_by_device`, so recording is necessary-but-not-sufficient to arm.\"\"\"\n96\t        from ..gesture.session import ARM_REQUEST, _ARM_CORE, arm_request_message\n97\t        from ..reuse import verify_one\n98\t        authorized = self._authorized()\n99\t        if request.get(\"signal\") != ARM_REQUEST:\n100\t            raise ValueError(\"not an arm request\")\n101\t        pub = request.get(\"pubkey\")\n102\t        if pub not in authorized:\n103\t            raise ValueError(\"signing device is not authorized\")\n104\t        core = {k: request.get(k) for k in _ARM_CORE}\n105\t        try:                                            # verify_one RAISES on a malformed-length sig — refuse cleanly\n106\t            ok = verify_one(pub, arm_request_message(core), request.get(\"sig\", \"\"))\n107\t        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n108\t            ok = False\n109\t        if not ok:\n110\t            raise ValueError(\"arm request signature invalid\")\n111\t        sig = request.get(\"sig\")\n112\t        # Best-effort dedup OUTSIDE the append lock, over a BOUNDED recent window (see submit_device_approval).\n113\t        for r in self.store.tail(_DEDUP_WINDOW):\n114\t            p = r.payload\n115\t            if p.get(\"signal\") == ARM_REQUEST and p.get(\"pubkey\") == pub and p.get(\"sig\") == sig:\n116\t                return r.seq                            # already recorded — idempotent, no spine bloat\n117\t        # record ONLY the signed core + pubkey + sig (never `**request` — no unsigned extras persisted)\n118\t        return self.store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"mesh\", actor=\"DEVICE\",\n119\t                                 payload={\"signal\": ARM_REQUEST, \"device_id\": core[\"device_id\"],\n120\t                                          \"nonce\": core[\"nonce\"], \"ts\": core[\"ts\"],\n121\t                                          \"ttl_seconds\": core[\"ttl_seconds\"], \"pubkey\": pub, \"sig\": sig,\n122\t                                          \"tier\": \"A0\", \"decision\": \"auto\"})\n123\t\n124\t    def panic_engage(self, *, by: str = \"phone\") -> int:\n125\t        \"\"\"Halt the mesh from the phone. ANY engage halts (fail-safe) — no signature needed for the\n126\t        SAFE direction. Release stays owner-only at the desktop (the dangerous direction is signed).\"\"\"\n127\t        from ..governor.killswitch import SIGNAL as KS_SIGNAL\n128\t        return self.store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"mesh\", actor=\"DEVICE\",\n129\t                                 payload={\"signal\": KS_SIGNAL, \"state\": \"engaged\", \"by\": by,\n130\t                                          \"reason\": \"panic halt from phone\", \"tier\": \"A0\", \"decision\": \"auto\"})\n131\t\n132\t    def relay(self, text: str) -> str:\n133\t        \"\"\"Relay a KERNEL command — the same T0-router + WARDEN gate + signed action log as voice/UI.\"\"\"\n134\t        from ..voice.dispatch import KernelDispatch\n135\t        return KernelDispatch().send(text)\n136\t"}]},"uuid":"5c8aaaec-6ca9-4cbd-a173-936a3a7d7c63","timestamp":"2026-07-19T06:47:48.011Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"265f6ccf-c6db-474a-be08-3bfbaf0bdd9e","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

Concurrency: chain intact, seqs contiguous, no fork (HIGH-2 holds; the 8-way identical-replay double-record is the pre-existing, documented outside-lock best-effort behavior — old full-scan raced identically, not a regression).\n\n**BLOCK-1 (MEDIUM DoS + Honesty overclaim).** `sigil/bridge/daemon.py:19,84,113` + docstring `sigil/spine/store.py:124-127`. The bounded window makes replay-dedup **non-idempotent across the window boundary**. An attacker holding a **fixed pool of ≥ `_DEDUP_WINDOW`+1 distinct captured *valid signed* bodies** (arm requests or approvals — no private key needed) can rotate-replay them for **unbounded** spine growth, ~1 record per request, generating **zero** new signatures. Repro (`scratchpad/repro_change2_sec.py`), window patched to 8 for a cheap crisp boundary + confirmed at the real 2048:\n\n```\npool = 9 (=window+1), replay the SAME 9 bodies 5 rounds -> records: [9,18,27,36,45]  (unbounded)\npool = 8 (=window),   replay the SAME 8 bodies 5 rounds -> records: [8,8,8,8,8]        (bounded)\nreal window 2048: submit 2049 -> 2049 records; replay 200 aged-out bodies -> +200 records\n```\n\nThe old `iter_records()` full scan bounded replay-bloat to *the number of distinct captured bodies, forever*, no matter how many requests were sent. The diff's justifications — \"a flood is always recent, so the window catches it\" (daemon.py:83), \"no spine bloat\" (daemon.py:116), and the `tail` docstring \"a replay whose original has aged out of the window creates at most ONE duplicate\" (store.py:126-127) — are **true for a single body but false in aggregate**: a *different* aged-out pool member creates another duplicate, and rotating the pool makes every replay create one. This is exactly the \"must not re-open the bloat sink\" property the surrounding code was written to hold; the comment now asserts an anti-bloat guarantee the code no longer enforces. Per RED-PEN honesty doctrine (overclaiming what the deterministic layer enforces) this blocks independent of exploit difficulty.\n\nScope/severity honesty: preconditions are stiff (≥2049 distinct valid signed bodies; WireGuard-plaintext capture; an authorized, non-revoked pubkey) and impact is **disk/audit-log DoS only** — recording a stale arm request does **not** arm (freshness+replay-nonce still gate `arm_by_device`), and the hash chain stays valid. The spine has **no size cap or rotation** (confirmed), so the bloat is a real, if slow, resource-exhaustion path.
